verified_facts: NASA states the challenge opened August 19, 2026 and the official host currently labels submissions open.
Phase 1 registration closes October 28, 2026 at 5:00 p.m. ET and Phase 1 submissions close November 11, 2026 at 5:00 p.m. ET.

The official host states a $2 million total award pool. Up to four Phase 1 winners receive $200,000 each; qualifying teams may receive an additional $200,000 in Phase 2 and $100,000 in Phase 3, for up to $500,000 per winner across three phases.
NASA intends to offer each team that successfully completes Phase 3 an orbital flight test at no cost.
Individuals must be U.S. citizens or U.S. permanent residents and at least 18 years old.
Organizations must be incorporated in and maintain a primary place of business in the United States.
Teams must be composed of otherwise eligible participants and led by a U.S. citizen or permanent resident who is at least 18 years old.

Foreign nationals may participate only under specified eligible relationships, acknowledgement requirements, and applicable trade/export-law compliance; they are not themselves eligible to receive a NASA prize.
Each eligible lead applicant may submit one application, while serving as a partner on another distinct application is permitted under the stated rules.
Applicants cannot receive duplicate U.S. government funding for the same scope of work; government-funded development can affect eligibility and IP rights.

Participants must have at least $250,000 in liability insurance or otherwise demonstrate financial responsibility for that amount. Proof is required when identified as a potential winner and the coverage must meet the official challenge conditions.
The participant retains ownership of inventions, software, and authored work arising from the challenge; NASA may negotiate for a license to use resulting solutions.
Standalone free-flying satellites are not eligible. Every delivered solution must be compatible with operation as a hosted payload on a commercial spacecraft.

Phase 1 valid submissions receive five expert reviews scored on a 1-5 rubric with normalization; top-scoring submissions proceed to a selection committee that selects up to four winners using judging results plus programmatic considerations.
The challenge is a prize competition rather than a grant; prize funds are distributed directly to winners and may be used at the winner's discretion subject to continuing eligibility.
Official FAQ says parts of a submission such as technology title and description may be published, while applicants may choose to exclude confidential or sensitive information from their submission.

direct_entry_cost.registration_fee_evidence: No registration or submission fee is stated on the reviewed official challenge, FAQ, rules, timeline, evaluation, insurance, or technical-guideline pages.
material_participation_costs: At least $250,000 liability-insurance coverage or equivalent demonstrated financial responsibility is required.

Teams are responsible for developing the hardware and completing the required build/test work; NASA covers the intended Phase 3 orbital flight-test opportunity but not ordinary solution-development costs.

finding.authorization_scope_note: This is a legitimate prize challenge, not a security-testing authorization. Nothing in these materials authorizes testing of NASA, commercial spacecraft, or third-party systems outside the competition's published submission activities.
remaining_verification_before_structured: Preserve the complete Phase 1 submission form and mandatory field/format limits before assigning build work.
Confirm the intended participant or team actually satisfies U.S. eligibility and can meet the $250,000 financial-responsibility requirement.

If foreign-national teammates are contemplated, preserve the Foreign Participant Acknowledgement Form and confirm applicable export/trade restrictions for the specific team composition and technology.
Before committing substantial work, review any Award Force platform terms that materially affect submission or data handling.

A structured active case should still wait until the Phase 1 submission form is preserved and participant eligibility/financial responsibility are confirmed.
